plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-14 from the official Salem College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (current edition, catoid=34), Health Science Major (BA) program page (poid=914). Salem College publishes major requirements but no official semester sequence for this program (its Print Degree Planner is a blank worksheet), so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block. The recorded total is the program requirement as printed on the program page; the full degree requirements, including the Salem Impact core (published separately in the same catalog), are not itemized here. Per-course credits are the Hour(s) values printed on each course's own official course detail page in the same catalog; the program page itself prints no per-course credits. Prerequisites naming courses outside this plan are disclosed in these notes and are not recorded as plan prerequisites. Courses titled 'with Lab' carry separate 0-Hour(s) lab corequisites in the catalog, disclosed in these notes and not placed as separate courses. Catalog anomaly, transcribed as printed and not corrected: CHEM 120's detail page prints its prerequisite as 'XXX 111', a course that does not exist in this catalog, so CHEM 120 carries no recorded prerequisite; the same 'XXX 111' string appears in the printed prerequisites of HSCI 200, HSCI 290 and HSCI 370. The catalog states the BA requires 65 to 71 hours of coursework, of which 46 to 49 hours are in the science, mathematics and data interpretation core and the advanced science courses. The recorded total (71) is the printed maximum, exercised as: core 35 (fixed 31 + statistics slot at 4, the value at which the core sums to its printed 35 hours) + advanced science 14 + experiential 10 (the block's printed total) + interdisciplinary perspectives 12 (the block's printed total) = 71; core + advanced = 49, the printed science maximum. At itemized minimums (statistics at 3, advanced at 11, HSCI 270 at 1) the same itemization sums to exactly the printed 65 minimum. STRUCTURAL READING, disclosed: the five ethics courses printed under Interdisciplinary Perspectives carry no choose wording on the page, but the printed 12-hour block total and the printed 65-hour degree minimum both hold only if that list is choose-one (see the ethics slot note); recorded on that reading, not silently. Advanced science exercise: the Understanding Disease slot is recorded at 3 listing the two 3-Hour(s) PUBH options, with the three 4-Hour(s) BIOL options (BIOL 225 Parasitology, BIOL 235 Microbiology with Lab, BIOL 280 Immunology) disclosed on the slot; the Advanced Natural Science slots are recorded at 4 listing the five 4-Hour(s) options, with BIOL 310 Advanced Genetics (3) and BIOL 312 Genetic Explorations (2) disclosed on the slots. The catalog's printed lab corequisites in this plan are BIOL 100L, BIOL 101L, BIOL 205L (when BIOL 205 is the statistics choice), BIOL 218L, BIOL 219L, CHEM 110L, CHEM 120L, CHEM 201L, CHEM 202L and PHYS 210L / PHYS 220L (when the physics courses are taken), each 0 Hour(s). Catalog anomalies disclosed, not corrected: HHMN 320's detail states it is cross-listed with RELI 320, but no RELI 320 exists in this catalog (established in Wave90 by catalog search); the BA page spells one heading 'Indisciplinary' [sic]; PUBH 260's title is spelled 'Intoduction' [sic]. The introduction states students are expected to take HSCI 070 and consult with their adviser before choosing elective courses. No residency note is printed for this program.

courses.title: Internship in Health Science
courses.choice_note: Required in the Experiential Learning and Professional Development block. Printed at 1-4 Hour(s) on its detail page and recorded here at 3, the value at which the block sums to its printed 10 hours (1 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 3); at 1 hour the block totals 8 and at 4 hours it totals 11, as printed. Its description states it is open to sophomores, juniors and seniors with at least a 2.0 cumulative GPA, the maximum in any term is five semester hours, and admission is by application only.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives: Ethics
courses.choice_note: Choose one course for the ethics part of the Interdisciplinary Perspectives Courses block. The program page prints the five ethics courses after 'Required: SOCI 100' with no subheading and no choose wording; the block's printed total of 12 hours holds only as SOCI 100 (3) + one ethics course (3) + the Written and Oral Communication choose-one (3) + the Cultural Awareness choose-one (3), and at itemized minimums the whole degree then sums to exactly the catalog's printed 65-hour minimum, so the block is recorded on that reading and the ambiguity is disclosed here and in the plan notes. All five options are printed at 3 Hour(s), in printed order. HHMN 215 is cross-listed with WGSS 215 and RELI 215 (neither is a separate option in this block, as printed); HHMN 320's detail states a cross-listing with RELI 320, which does not exist in this catalog (see plan notes).

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Written and Oral Communication
courses.choice_note: Choose one course for the Interdisciplinary Written and Oral Communication block (the BA page spells the heading 'Indisciplinary' [sic]). All twelve catalog options are printed at 3 Hour(s), in printed order. HHMN 248 / HIST 248 are a cross-listed pair, counted once; ENGL 255 / HHMN 255 are a cross-listed pair (the cross-listing is stated on HHMN 255's detail page only); NFPM 130 / SOCI 130 are a cross-listed pair (SOCI 130's detail prints a self-referential cross-listing, as printed). HIST 282's and NFPM 130's and SOCI 130's titles are truncated as printed in the catalog display.
